title: Biology and biomedicine — Friday, 20 November 2026 arXiv batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance-ranked snapshot from an incomplete biomedical preprint corpus. Attention evidence was sparse, and this is not a most-read or most-downloaded ranking.

sections.title: Headline
sections.abstract: 12 notable recent papers. The batch centers on computational molecular and biomedical methods: protein/RNA design, molecular and genomic inference, multi-omics/pathology, and medical imaging. Ranked by relevance and reported evaluation, not popularity.

sections.title: ShEPhERD-score: Fast, adaptable three-dimensional alignment of molecular features
sections.abstract: The authors combine differentiable 3D molecular similarity representations with CPU/GPU kernels for high-throughput alignment and screening, reporting competitive DUDE-Z results and up to 1.03 million alignments per second on one GPU.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present a unified, modular and differentiable toolkit for 3D molecular alignment and screening; target-wise results indicate no single scoring mode wins across targets.
sections.unique_caveat: Computational benchmark evidence only, not prospective compound testing or experimental evidence of binding or efficacy; the best scoring mode varies by target.

sections.title: The Montparnasse Algorithm for RNA Design
sections.abstract: The v2 paper reports a Monte Carlo search algorithm for inverse RNA folding that solved a median 96 of 100 Eterna100 V1 targets over five runs, versus 90 for DesiRNA under the same folding model and budget.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author reports improved search coverage and speed on Eterna100 V1 using a shared ViennaRNA 1.8.5/Turner 1999 objective.
sections.unique_caveat: Computational folding under one energy model; it does not establish that designed RNAs fold as intended in biochemical experiments or cells.

sections.title: A General Harness for Protein Foundation Model Fitness Prediction
sections.abstract: The v2 work adds MSA retrieval and structure-aware score corrections to frozen protein-model predictions, reporting improved rank correlations across three variant benchmarks covering 1,211 assays and 3.1 million measured variants.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors’ training-free VenusREM-Harness combines model scores with evolutionary and structural evidence; they report gains across 71 configurations and an average ProteinGym Spearman of 0.556 for VenusREM2.
sections.unique_caveat: Retrospective benchmark results, not prospective protein-engineering experiments; performance depends on benchmark composition, homolog coverage and chosen assays.

sections.title: Ab-initio cryo-EM reconstruction from moments of denoised images
sections.abstract: The authors use the first three moments of denoised particle images to initialize cryo-EM reconstruction without estimating each particle orientation, reporting successful refinement starts on six experimental datasets.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors’ MoMDeni method estimates an ab-initio model from denoised-image moments, avoiding explicit orientation estimation and allowing non-uniform viewing directions.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors call the experimental results preliminary; denoising biases moment estimates, loses fine structure, and the method can fail for low-molecular-weight targets.

sections.title: An Explainable and Scalable Hierarchical Tensor Framework for Integrating Multi-Omics and Digital Pathomics
sections.abstract: HIT-Fuse combines six molecular and pathology modalities across four TCGA cancer cohorts and reports survival stratification, cohort-dependent prediction gains and database-based support for some decoded drivers.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose hierarchical tensor fusion with missing-modality reconstruction and traceable attributions; they report a 56.4% relative weighted-F1 increase for glioma after cohort expansion.
sections.unique_caveat: The evaluation uses TCGA-derived cohorts and computational/database cross-checks; it is not independent clinical validation, and reconstructed modalities may affect cohort composition and performance.

sections.title: From Sequence Uncertainty to Phenotype Hypotheses: Uncertainty-Conditioned Inference over Biomedical Knowledge Graphs
sections.abstract: The authors propagate genomic-model uncertainty into graph-supported phenotype-hypothesis distributions and report held-out association recovery on AlzKB and Hetionet.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce an uncertainty-conditioned path-energy method to allocate probability across gene–disease–phenotype routes without patient-level phenotype supervision.
sections.unique_caveat: Computational hypothesis ranking, not diagnosis or clinical validation; the authors note the gene-holdout advantage is driven mainly by three genes and is not established for all genes.

sections.title: Dynamical Variational Theory of Stochastic Reaction Networks
sections.abstract: A Plefka-expansion variational method approximates non-Markovian dynamics and fluctuations in stochastic reaction networks, with tests on gene regulation, enzyme kinetics and infection models.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors derive a tractable dynamical variational approximation for general stoichiometries and time-varying rates, including a self-consistent bubble resummation.
sections.unique_caveat: Reported support is numerical benchmarking against model systems, not direct experimental validation of a biochemical mechanism.

sections.title: OpenTME: An Open Dataset of AI-powered H&E Tumor Microenvironment Profiles from TCGA
sections.abstract: The v2 release describes AI-derived tumor-microenvironment profiles for 5,268 TCGA whole-slide images across ten cancer types, with more than 20,000 quantitative readouts per slide.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors release an open-access, living dataset of model-generated cell, tissue and spatial-neighborhood readouts for computational tumor-microenvironment research.
sections.unique_caveat: Readouts inherit the underlying AI models’ errors; the paper notes limited cancer-type coverage and that detailed spatial coordinates are not included in the public release.

sections.title: When Foundation Models Disagree: Representational Heterogeneity for Calibrated Uncertainty in Whole-Slide Image Classification
sections.abstract: CALIFUSE uses disagreement among pathology foundation-model representations to estimate confidence and reports improved calibration and misclassification detection across seven whole-slide-image tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use between-encoder representational heterogeneity and chunk-level evidence agreement as uncertainty cues, without training an additional fusion module.
sections.unique_caveat: Benchmark evaluation; calibration and selective-prediction results do not establish clinical utility or transfer to other institutions and scanners.

sections.title: GraphEP: A Calibrated Data System and Benchmark for Learning Cardiac Electrophysiology
sections.abstract: GraphEP packages 732 simulated cardiac electrophysiology trajectories across 20 anatomies and benchmarks graph and physiology-informed models for predicting transmembrane potential.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide a reproducible graph-native dataset and report that physiology-informed models perform best on complementary prediction metrics.
sections.unique_caveat: The benchmark is based on mechanistic simulations rather than measured patient electrophysiology; model performance does not demonstrate clinical readiness.

sections.title: Towards consensus on practical probabilistic evaluation metrics for clinical decision making in radiotherapy
sections.abstract: The authors evaluate probabilistic robustness metrics for proton radiotherapy using 60 treatment plans from three Dutch centers and interviews with eight radiation oncologists.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors compare probabilistic metrics with current robustness evaluation and report that interviewed oncologists considered them suitable, while metric preferences varied.
sections.unique_caveat: Plan-based evaluation plus interviews, not a trial showing improved patient outcomes; the authors call for further consensus and clinical validation before broad implementation.

sections.title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning for Shear Wave Speed Estimation in MR Elastography
sections.abstract: An end-to-end physics-informed reconstruction and inversion method estimates shear-wave speed from undersampled MRE data, reporting a 30% NRMSE reduction versus total-variation minimization and evaluation on in-vivo data.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors jointly train reconstruction and phase-gradient inversion to estimate tissue shear-wave speed directly from k-space.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evaluation is retrospective and does not establish multi-site generalization or improved clinical decisions; the in-vivo sample size is not stated in the abstract.
sections.comment: Accepted version published in IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering (2026), early access

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.abstract: Computational molecular design and protein/RNA scoring; data-driven molecular and cancer representations; uncertainty-aware biomedical prediction; physics-informed and mechanistic modeling.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.abstract: Prospectively validate RNA/protein design against biochemical assays; stress-test cryo-EM methods under realistic noise; evaluate omics/pathology transfer and calibration on independent cohorts; test medical-physics methods in external and prospective workflows.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.abstract: The batch is strongest in computational molecular design, molecular/genomic modeling and imaging methods. Attention signals were too sparse to support a popularity chart; reported benchmark and retrospective evidence should not be confused with broad clinical validation.
